caption: The drawing depicts a single metal lantern positioned upright on a flat, light tan background. The lantern has a cylindrical base with small, evenly spaced star-shaped cutouts close to the bottom edge. Above the base, a glass enclosure surrounds the central lamp mechanism, which includes a circular burner and a visible wick knob. Surrounding the glass body are four arched metal wires forming a protective frame that connects at four points around the midsection. The top of the lantern features a domed metal cap with ventilation holes and a rounded carrying handle attached to two small loops. The handle is slightly arched and features a thicker, cylindrical grip at the top. The entire drawing is rendered in grayscale, with shading to indicate metallic texture and reflection. The background paper shows some discoloration, faint stains, and remnants of tape at the corners. In the lower right corner, the artist’s name “Alfred Farrell” is inscribed in small, delicate letters.
title: Coal Oil Lantern
cluster: #16 — Lighting Devices: Lamps, Lanterns, and Candleholders
